matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After proposing a transformed equation, convert each Roman numeral to its integer value and verify that the arithmetic relation holds. Without this check, you may accept a visually plausible but mathematically false equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have identified a possible single‑stick move and formed the new equation.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformation that yields ‘III = XII - IX’ without confirming that 3 = 12 − 9.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you may only place it on a target character if the orientation matches the character’s required orientation. Ignoring orientation leads to invalid numerals or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider moving a stick from one character to another.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from ‘+’ onto a ‘V’ and treating it as a diagonal, producing an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: The single‑stick move may affect only the source character (which loses the stick) and the destination character (which gains the stick). Changing more than two characters violates the puzzle rule.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During the planning of a stick move; ensure only two characters are altered.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from ‘+’ and also deleting a stick from ‘=’ without adding it elsewhere, effectively changing three characters.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: Only specific numeral pairs can be interconverted by moving a single stick (e.g., I↔II↔III, V↔X, L↔I, IV↔VI). Use these known transformations to adjust numeral values while preserving stick counts and orientations.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change a numeral’s value and a known single‑stick transformation exists.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘IV’ to ‘VI’ by moving the vertical stick from the left side of the V to the right side, without altering any other character.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The response must be a single line that begins with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ (case‑insensitive) and contains the final equation with no extra text. Missing the prefix or adding extra lines causes the answer to be rejected.
matchstick.example: Providing only ‘IX = V + IV’ without the required prefix.

matchstick.title: Accurate parsing of the original equation
matchstick.principle: Record each numeral and operator exactly as they appear (including order and spacing) before attempting any transformation. Mis‑parsing can lead to moving sticks from the wrong character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of the problem, before any reasoning.
matchstick.example: Treating the ‘-’ in ‘XII - IV’ as a ‘+’ and moving a stick accordingly.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a ‘‑’ creates a ‘+’; removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ yields a ‘‑’. This allows you to change addition to subtraction (or vice‑versa) with a single stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the arithmetic gap suggests flipping a ‘+’ to ‘‑’ or the reverse could balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Turning ‘+’ into ‘‑’ by removing its vertical stick but forgetting to add that stick elsewhere.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer from '+' to numeral (adds I)
matchstick.principle: Removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ (turning it into ‘‑’) and adding that vertical stick to a numeral that needs an extra vertical line (e.g., I → II) increases the numeral’s value by one while preserving the total stick count.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a small increase (by 1) in a numeral’s value can close the numeric gap.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from ‘+’ to the ‘V’ in ‘VIII’ without checking that V can accept a vertical stick, resulting in an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via horizontal stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Removing one horizontal line from ‘=’ turns it into ‘‑’; adding that horizontal line to a ‘‑’ creates ‘=’. This lets you swap equality for subtraction (or vice‑versa) with a single stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a value that could be fixed by changing ‘=’ to ‘‑’ or the reverse.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal from ‘=’ but forgetting to place it on a ‘‑’, leaving a stray stick.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual transformation and forgets to check whether the resulting Roman‑numeral equation is mathematically true.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the integer values of all numerals after the move and confirm that the arithmetic relation holds before outputting the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving a stick, the model may ignore the required orientation or the number of sticks a Roman numeral needs, producing a shape that does not correspond to any valid numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Refer to the list of allowed single‑stick numeral transformations and ensure the source and destination characters remain valid after the move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may change the equality sign to a non‑equality operator (e.g., ‘≠’) or combine sticks in a way that yields an undefined operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only convert operators among ‘+’, ‘‑’, and ‘=’ using the allowed vertical or horizontal stick moves; never introduce other symbols.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character but does not place it on another character, effectively deleting a stick, which violates the puzzle rule.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When you take a stick from a source, immediately decide which character will receive it and ensure that character stays valid after the addition.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model outputs only the equation or adds extra commentary, omitting the required prefix ‘Correct version of the equation:’.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Write the final line exactly as ‘Correct version of the equation: <equation>’ with no additional text.
